planting.note: Plant tubers horizontally, growing tip up, in heavy clay soil without added organic matter, in a wide, shallow, undrained container submerged just a few inches below the water surface in full sun; Chawan Basu is one of the classic dwarf bowl lotus cultivars for small container water gardens.

directions: Chawan Basu, whose name translates roughly to teacup lotus, is one of the most popular dwarf bowl lotus cultivars for small-scale water gardening, staying compact enough to bloom well in a half-barrel or large glazed bowl rather than needing a full pond. Its single flowers open white with a soft pink blush concentrated at the petal tips, held above the rounded, blue-green, umbrella-like leaves typical of lotus, and it flowers repeatedly through the warm season once established. Feed with aquatic plant fertilizer tablets during the growing season, and in zones with hard winter freezes, move the container to a frost-free space or sink it below the ice line for winter protection, since lotus tubers are more cold-sensitive than most hardy water lilies.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

common_name: Comanche Water Lily (Changeable Peach-to-Copper Hardy Water Lily)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes in heavy clay soil in a wide, shallow container submerged 12-24 inches below the water surface in full sun; Comanche is a classic changeable-color Marliac-type water lily, its flower color shifting noticeably over the several days each bloom is open.

directions: Comanche is a classic changeable hardy water lily, opening a warm peachy-apricot on its first day and deepening through copper-orange to a rich burnt-red-orange by the final day of bloom, giving a single planting a constantly shifting color display over its bloom cycle. The cupped flowers are held over mottled, purple-flecked green foliage typical of the older Marliac-bred hardy water lily lines. Divide rhizomes every two to three years when they crowd their container, and feed during the growing season with aquatic plant fertilizer tablets pushed into the soil for the strongest, most reliable bloom.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

common_name: Pink Sensation Water Lily (Vigorous Deep Pink Hardy Water Lily)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes in heavy clay soil in a wide, shallow container submerged 12-24 inches below the water surface in full sun; Pink Sensation is a vigorous grower and benefits from a larger container than more compact water lily cultivars.

directions: Pink Sensation is a vigorous, free-flowering hardy water lily prized for its rich, deep pink, star-shaped flowers held well above the water surface, a stronger, more saturated pink than many older hardy cultivars, opening reliably even in the heat of a Gulf South summer. Its robust growth quickly fills a pond or large container with attractive round green pads, providing shade cover for fish as well as flowers, and it tends to bloom more heavily and over a longer season than more compact cultivars. Divide rhizomes every two to three years when they crowd their container, and feed during the growing season with aquatic plant fertilizer tablets pushed into the soil for the best bloom.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

common_name: Helvola Water Lily (Miniature Yellow Hardy Water Lily)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes in heavy clay soil in a wide, shallow container submerged only 4-12 inches below the water surface in full sun; Helvola is one of the smallest hardy water lily cultivars and is well suited to a half-barrel, small tub, or shallow container garden rather than a deep pond.

directions: Helvola is among the smallest and most widely grown miniature hardy water lily cultivars, producing tiny, star-shaped, soft canary-yellow flowers only 2 inches across over small, mottled, purple-speckled leaves, on a plant scaled for a shallow tub, small container pond, or even a large decorative bowl rather than a full-sized pond. Its diminutive size makes lotus- and water-lily-growing accessible to gardeners without room for a large water feature, and it flowers freely through the warm season once established in shallow, undrained water. Divide rhizomes every couple of years as the small container becomes crowded, and feed during the growing season with aquatic plant fertilizer tablets for the best bloom.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society

common_name: Joey Tomocik Water Lily (Vigorous Bright Yellow Heat-Tolerant Hardy Water Lily)

planting.note: Plant rhizomes in heavy clay soil in a wide, shallow container submerged 12-24 inches below the water surface in full sun; Joey Tomocik is noted for continuing to bloom heavily through hot summer water temperatures that slow many other hardy water lily cultivars.

directions: Joey Tomocik is a vigorous hardy water lily bearing bright, clear yellow, star-shaped flowers held well above the water on strong stems, standing out from the more muted creamy-yellow tones of older yellow-flowered cultivars. It is particularly valued for continuing to flower heavily through the hottest stretch of summer, when the bloom of many other hardy water lilies slows or stalls, making it a strong performer for warm Gulf South ponds. Divide rhizomes every two to three years when they crowd their container, and feed during the growing season with aquatic plant fertilizer tablets pushed into the soil for the best, most continuous bloom.
sources: International Waterlily and Water Gardening Society
